name: Asadi of Tus
credit: Sadiqi Beg, Garshasp fighting the sagsars, from a Garshaspnama manuscript (1573), British Library Or. 12985, f. 45v · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Abu Nasr Ali ibn Ahmad Asadi Tusi was a Persian poet of the eleventh century, a native of Tus in Khorasan, the same town that produced Firdausi. He is said to have moved west and to have lived at courts in Azerbaijan and Arran, and he died around 1072.

His best-known work is the Garshaspnameh, an epic of some nine thousand couplets completed in 1066 that tells the deeds of the hero Garshasp, an ancestor of Rustam. He is also credited with the Lughat-e Furs, among the earliest surviving Persian dictionaries, and with a group of verse debates (munazara) between pairs such as night and day, or Arab and Persian.
